'''Jacek Banasiak''' (born 15 March 1959) is a Polish mathematician who is a Professor and [[South African Research Chair]] in Mathematical Models and Methods in Biosciences and Bioengineering at the [[University of Pretoria]], South Africa.

== Early life and education ==
Jacek Banasiak was born on 15 March 1959 in [[Łódź]], Poland.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORCID |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-3381-0774 |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=orcid.org}}</ref> He obtained a [[Master of Science]] (MSc) in Math from the [[Łódź University of Technology]] in 1981,<ref name=":1" /> and [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) in mathematics on 15 March 1989 from the [[University of Strathclyde]], Scotland.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nowa Nauka Polska |url=https://nauka-polska.pl/#/profile/research?id=89711&_k=oyzgp4 |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=nauka-polska.pl}}</ref> He was [[Habilitation|hablitated]] (PD) in Physics on 17 June 1999 from the Faculty of Mathematics, Informatics and Mechanics, [[University of Warsaw]] with a thesis titled ''Singularly Perturbed Evolution Equations with Applications in Kinetic Theory and Other Branches of Mathematical Physics''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nowa Nauka Polska |url=https://nauka-polska.pl/#/profile/research?id=8053&_k=7k0pre |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=nauka-polska.pl}}</ref>
 
== Career and research ==
Banasiak became a professor on 21 December 2007,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Nowa Nauka Polska |url=https://nauka-polska.pl/#/profile/scientist?id=74107&_k=81bc9d |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=nauka-polska.pl}}</ref> and has been a Professor of Mathematical Sciences at the [[University of KwaZulu-Natal]] from 2011 until 2015.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Scientific Committee |url=https://www.pacom2022.com/program/committees |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=PAN AFRICAN CONGRESS OF MATHEMATICIANS 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacek Banasiak {{!}} African Institute for Mathematical Sciences - Academia.edu |url=https://aims.academia.edu/JacekBanasiak |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=aims.academia.edu}}</ref> After, he joined the [[University of Pretoria]] and became the [[South African Research Chair]] in Mathematical Models and Methods in Biosciences and Bioengineering at the Department of Mathematics and Applied Mathematics,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacek Banasiak {{!}} University of Pretoria |url=https://www.up.ac.za/jacek-banasiak |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=www.up.ac.za}}</ref> [[extraordinary professor]] at the Łódź University of Technology,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof J (Jacek) Banasiak {{!}} Article {{!}} University of Pretoria |url=https://www.up.ac.za/mathematics-and-applied-mathematics/article/2229299/prof-j-jacek-banasiak |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=www.up.ac.za |language=en}}</ref> and a [[Visiting scholar|visiting professor]] of [[Mathematics]] and [[Statistics]] at the Strathclyde University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof Jacek Banasiak {{!}} University of Strathclyde |url=https://www.strath.ac.uk/staff/banasiakjacekprof/ |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=www.strath.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

Banasiak research focuses on [[applied mathematics]] especially [[semigroup]] theory,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacek Banasiak |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=ufHvf1IAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2022-12-25 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref> [[asymptotic analysis]],<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Banasiak |first1=Jacek |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9NrsCgAAQBAJ |title=Singularly Perturbed Evolution Equations With Applications To Kinetic Theory |last2=Mika |first2=Janusz R. |date=1995-10-24 |publisher=World Scientific |isbn=978-981-4500-97-5 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Mika |first1=J. Banasiak served as the vice president of the [[South African Mathematical Society]] (2001–2005).<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Banasiak |url=https://africanscientists.africa/business-directory/banasiak/ |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=African Scientists Directory |language=en-US}}</ref> He is a member of the [[Academy of Science of South Africa]] and the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] (AIMS).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Prof. Jacek Banasiak – AIMS South Africa |url=https://aims.ac.za/researcher/prof-jacek-banasiak/ |access-date=2022-12-24 |language=en-US}}</ref> He is also the Editor-in-Chief of [[Afrika Matematica|Afrika Matematika]] since 2010,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Afrika Matematika |url=https://www.springer.com/journal/13370 |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=Springer |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> Associate Editor of Quaestiones Mathematicae<ref>{{Cite web |title=Quaestiones Mathematicae |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/action/journalInformation?show=editorialBoard&journalCode=tqma20& |access-date=2022-12-25 |website=Taylor & Francis |language=en}}</ref> and Evolution Equations and Control Theory (EECT),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editorial Board {{!}} Evolution Equations and Control Theory |url=https://www.aimsciences.org/eect/editorialboard}}</ref> and a member of the Editorial Board of Mathematical Methods for the Applied Sciences<ref>{{Cite web |title=Editorial Board {{!}} Mathematical Methods in the Applied Sciences |doi=10.1002/(ISSN)1099-1476 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/10991476/homepage/editorialboard.html}}</ref> and Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Differential Equations and Dynamical Systems |url=https://www.springer.com/journal/12591/editors |access-date=2022-12-25 |website=Springer |language=en |archive-date=2022-12-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221225014705/https://www.springer.com/journal/12591/editors |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
In 2012, Banasiak won the South African Mathematical Society (SAMS) award for Research Distinction.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Award winners – SAMS |url=http://www.sams.ac.za/award-winners-sams/ |access-date=2022-12-24 |language=en-US |archive-date=2022-12-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221224215306/http://www.sams.ac.za/award-winners-sams/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2014, he was honoured with the [[Cross of Merit (Poland)|Polish Cross of Merit]] (Silver) for his contributions to science.<ref name=":1" /> Banasiak was elected a Fellow of the [[African Academy of Sciences]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Banasiak Jacek {{!}} The AAS |url=https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/banasiak-jacek |access-date=2022-12-24 |website=www.aasciences.africa |archive-date=2022-12-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221224173238/https://www.aasciences.africa/fellow/banasiak-jacek |url-status=dead }}</ref>
